newsitem.title: UK: Guinness, Grandmet merger dreamed up over dinner.
newsitem.headline: Guinness, Grandmet merger dreamed up over dinner.

text.p: The 20-billion pound ($32.5 billion) merger of two of Britain's brewing and spirits groups on Monday was hatched out over dinner last month between the companies' chairmen who have been friends for years.
The chairman of Grand Metropolitan Plc, George Bull, said he pitched the idea when his long-time chum Tony Greener, chairman of Guinness plc, was over at his house for dinner on April 10.
"The discussions started because I invited Tony to dinner," Bull told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV).
He said the idea of some kind of co-operation between the two rival companies had been rumoured for some time.
"It was exactly at that dinner on that date that I put the proposition that perhaps it was time that we settled down to a serious discussion and consider the prospect and the possibility," Bull said.

Greener then went to Africa for a week where he mulled the idea over. Upon his return, the two men sat down to just three weeks of discussions culminating in one of the largest mergers in British history.

Bull said earlier, "Tony Greener and I have known each other for 17 years and have been in 'friendly conflict' with each other across the world, and therefore it's a matter of great pleasure now to come together."

The deal creates the world's seventh largest food and drinks company, GMG Brands, and the world's leading spirits and wine company with combined spirits sales of over 100 million cases. ($ = 0.615 British Pounds)
